forAuthors.metaDescription: Manuscript requirements, formatting guidelines and the article template for the international scientific conferences in Qarshi.
forAuthors.heading: For authors
forAuthors.intro: Manuscripts are accepted in Uzbek, English or Russian. Prepare your article according to the requirements below, using the template, and send it through the submission page.
forAuthors.structureIntro: Articles must contain, in this order:
forAuthors.structure1: Title of the article in capital letters;
forAuthors.structure3: Affiliation: organisation, city, country and email address;
forAuthors.structure4: Abstract in Uzbek, English and Russian;
forAuthors.structure5: Keywords in Uzbek, English and Russian;
forAuthors.formatting3: Margins of 2.5 cm on all sides;
forAuthors.formatting4: Times New Roman, 12 pt, single line spacing;
forAuthors.formatting5: Justified text with a paragraph indentation of 1.25 cm;
forAuthors.formatting7: Figures and tables numbered sequentially, each with a title.
forAuthors.templateBody: Prepare your manuscript on the basis of the template: it already contains the required structure and styles.
forAuthors.submitBody: Register first, then send the finished manuscript through the submission page before the deadline. The deadlines for each conference are listed on the deadlines page.

venue.metaDescription: The conferences take place at the University of Economics and Pedagogy in Qarshi, Uzbekistan. Country and city information, the university and the recommended hotel.
venue.heading: Venue and accommodation
venue.countryBody1: Uzbekistan, officially the Republic of Uzbekistan, is a country in Central Asia with a population of about 37 million people. Its capital is Tashkent, and the official language is Uzbek; Russian and English are widely used in academia and tourism. For centuries the territory of present-day Uzbekistan lay at the heart of the Great Silk Road, and the historic cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
venue.countryBody2: The climate is continental, with hot, dry summers and mild autumns. Early October — the time of the conferences — is one of the most pleasant seasons, with daytime temperatures around 20–25 °C.
venue.visaBody: Citizens of more than 90 countries, including most European Union member states, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Türkiye and the CIS countries, may enter Uzbekistan without a visa for stays of up to 30 days. Most other nationals can obtain an electronic visa online at e-visa.gov.uz.
venue.mapAlt: Map of Uzbekistan with Qarshi marked
venue.mapNote: Qarshi lies in the south of Uzbekistan, about 520 km from Tashkent.
venue.cityBody1: Qarshi is the administrative centre of the Qashqadaryo Region in southern Uzbekistan, with a population of about 280,000. The city is more than 2,700 years old: it grew up in the oasis of the Kashkadarya River, and caravans of the Great Silk Road once passed through it.
venue.cityBody2: Today Qarshi is a modern regional centre known for its universities, bazaars and monuments such as the Odina complex and the Koʻk Gumbaz mosque. The city is served by Karshi International Airport and by rail, including trains from Tashkent via Samarkand.
venue.universityBody1: The conferences are organised by the University of Economics and Pedagogy, based in Qarshi. The university trains specialists in economics, business, pedagogy, languages and related fields, and hosts scientific and academic events throughout the year.
venue.universityBody2: Its modern campus brings together lecture halls, laboratories and a research library. The university's academic staff, together with partner institutions from Uzbekistan and abroad, form the organising and programme committees of the conferences.
venue.universityImageAlt: Main building of the University of Economics and Pedagogy
venue.universityGalleryAlt: University of Economics and Pedagogy, photo {index}
venue.hotelBody1: The modern Grand Sarbon Hotel in Qarshi is the recommended place to stay for participants. The hotel has 43 comfortable rooms — from twin rooms to suites — each with air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a work desk and free Wi-Fi.
venue.hotelBody2: Guests can use the restaurant and bar, garden and terrace, gym, sauna and swimming pool. The hotel offers a buffet breakfast, room service, a 24-hour front desk, free private parking and airport transfers; Karshi International Airport is about 9 km away.
venue.hotelImageAlt: Main entrance of the Grand Sarbon Hotel
venue.travelBody: Qarshi is reached by air via Karshi International Airport (KSQ), with connections through Tashkent, or by rail — daily trains link Tashkent and Qarshi via Samarkand. Check the current visa requirements for your citizenship well before travelling.

photos.metaDescription: Cultural excursion program to Samarkand within the framework of the international scientific and practical conference “Current Issues of Science and Technology”.
photos.heading: Cultural excursion to Samarkand
photos.intro: Within the framework of the international scientific and practical conference “Current Issues of Science and Technology” (October 8–10, Karshi, Uzbekistan), participants are invited on a guided tour of Samarkand’s Silk Road landmarks.
photos.itineraryDescription: Six landmarks in one afternoon, from the Gur-i Amir Mausoleum to Shah-i-Zinda. Times are local and approximate; click any photo to view it full screen.

about.metaDescription: Aims, scientific sections and key facts of the international scientific conference held at the University of Economics and Pedagogy in Qarshi, Uzbekistan.
about.heading: About the conference
about.lead: The conference is devoted to current issues of science and technology in the exact, engineering, natural and humanities sciences, and to strengthening interdisciplinary integration and international scientific cooperation.
about.body1: The international scientific conference brings together researchers, lecturers, doctoral students and practitioners from universities, research institutes and industry to discuss current issues of science and technology and to exchange contemporary research findings.
about.body2: The scientific programme is organised into four sections — exact, engineering, natural and humanities sciences. Each section has its own list of topics and an organising committee that reviews the submitted abstracts and builds the section programme.
about.sectionsLead: Papers are presented within four scientific sections. Open a section to see its programme, deadlines and committee.

privacy.metaDescription: How personal data submitted through this website is collected, used and stored.
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.updated: Placeholder text. TODO: replace with the reviewed policy before launch.
privacy.s1Body: Through the registration, newsletter and contact forms we collect the details you enter: name, organisation, country, address, phone, email, and the title and abstract of your article.
privacy.s2Body: The data is used to organise the conference, issue certificates, publish the proceedings, and send programme information. The newsletter address is used only to send announcements.
privacy.s3Body: Form submissions are stored in a spreadsheet held in the organisers' account with a cloud provider, accessible only to the organising team.
privacy.s4Body: Registration data is kept for as long as the proceedings remain published. Newsletter addresses are kept until you unsubscribe.
privacy.s5Body: You may ask for a copy of your data, ask for it to be corrected, or ask for it to be deleted. Write to the email address on the contacts page.
privacy.s6Body: The site stores your language choice and your cookie decision in the browser. No advertising cookies are used.
